defect: The definition constrained each input-reading transition set to at most one member but omitted the same singleton condition for epsilon transitions, so it admitted nondeterministic epsilon branching.
correction_basis: Aho's Columbia lecture notes and the Linz-based Ole Miss notes both require delta(q,a,Z) to have at most one member for every input symbol and epsilon, with epsilon availability excluding all input-consuming alternatives; Gallier and Quaintance give the equivalent unique transition regime for each state and stack-symbol pair.

defect: The lemma incorrectly inferred uniqueness of every finite accepting prefix from uniqueness of the maximal computation; one deterministic run may visit an accepting configuration more than once after consuming its input.
correction_basis: The corrected DPDA definition makes the next move unique, which proves that finite computations are comparable by extension and that the maximal computation is unique. The downstream proposition now obtains unique accepting computations separately by making post-endmarker accepting states halting before applying the PDA-to-CFG construction.
